title: The surah without bismillah
hook: the only surah that doesn't open with bismillah, which scholars link to its opening in 9:1

segments.voice: Yesterday: if they incline to peace, and surah eight closed. Your line was incline to peace. Did you take the cup of tea? Today, surah nine, and something missing at its door. Day four hundred twenty-one.
screen: `IF THEY INCLINE TO PEACE — INCLINE TO PEACE.`

segments.voice: Way back on day two of this path, you learned bismillah: in the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Since then you've watched it stand at the top of every surah, a hundred and thirteen times, like a doorway you walk through without looking. Open a printed Qur'an to surah nine, and the doorway isn't there. The page goes straight from the last line of surah eight to the first line of surah nine. Reciters who begin there don't say it. Out of a hundred and fourteen surahs, this is the only one. People have been asking why for fourteen centuries.
screen: `BISMILLAH, A HUNDRED AND THIRTEEN TIMES.` → `SURAH NINE: NO DOORWAY.` → `ASKED FOR FOURTEEN CENTURIES.`

segments.voice: Surah nine has two names. At-Tawbah, Repentance, for the repentance it describes later on. And Bara'ah, from its first word, which means a release, a disavowal, a declared end to obligations. In Pickthall's words, it opens: “Freedom from obligation (is proclaimed) from Allah and His messenger toward those of the idolaters with whom ye made a treaty.” It's a proclamation about treaties that had been broken, read out at the pilgrimage in the ninth year after the emigration. And the verses that follow make an exception: those who kept their treaties are to be honored to the end of their term. Why no bismillah? Scholars give two main explanations. One comes from a report in which the young scholar Ibn Abbas asked the caliph Uthman this very question. Uthman answered that surah eight was among the early Medinan revelations and surah nine among the last, that their content was similar, and that the Prophet ﷺ died without making clear whether nine was part of eight. So the compilers set them side by side and left out the line between them. The second explanation is attributed to Ali: the bismillah is a promise of safety, and this surah opens with that safety withdrawn from treaty-breakers. Many scholars hold both explanations together. And here's a detail people love: the bismillah still appears a hundred and fourteen times in the Qur'an. Surah twenty-seven contains it inside a verse, in a letter from the prophet Sulayman. The count stays whole. Only the doorway here is silent, and the silence itself became something to study.
screen: `BARA'AH — A RELEASE, A DISAVOWAL.` · `TREATIES BROKEN, TREATIES KEPT.` · `UTHMAN'S ANSWER; ALI'S ANSWER.` · `STILL A HUNDRED AND FOURTEEN.` · then, large: `THE SILENCE SPEAKS.`

segments.voice: Sit, and breathe. Think of somewhere in your day where words are usually said, and today notice the gap instead: the greeting a coworker didn't give, the thank-you you skipped, the bismillah you forgot before eating. Don't fix it yet. Just notice that a missing word can say as much as a spoken one. Then pick one place today where you'll say the word, on purpose. The bell holds the time.
The surah without bismillah. At-Tawbah, also called Bara'ah: the one surah that opens without in the name of God, and the reasons scholars give. Today's word.
Your line: the silence speaks. Today, notice one missing word, in your speech or someone else's, and what its absence says. Day four hundred twenty-one.

howItsDone: When reciting surah nine from its beginning, Muslims do not say the bismillah; many begin with a'udhu billah instead, and in printed copies of the Qur'an the surah follows surah eight with no basmala line.

fork.setup: you're Ibn Abbas, and you ask Uthman why surahs eight and nine sit together with no bismillah between them. what does he say?
options: the Prophet died without making clear whether nine was part of eight.
it was too long to fit.
fork.reveal: their content was similar and the Prophet hadn't made clear whether they were one, so the compilers left out the line (Tirmidhi; Abu Dawud).

original.note: Arabic: a release, a disavowal; the first word of surah nine and one of its names.

trapdoor: what you thought: someone forgot a line.
what it means: the one surah that opens without bismillah, for reasons scholars trace to its content and its compilation.
what a scholar hears: Uthman's answer (Tirmidhi 3086; Abu Dawud 786) has a debated chain; Ali's 'aman' explanation is cited by al-Qurtubi; 27:30 keeps the count at 114.
